title: core: Add SubViewportContainer child viewport transform virtual

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body: Lets a `SubViewportContainer` subclass tell the engine where it draws its child `SubViewport`, so mouse input, hover tracking and `get_screen_transform()` match the drawn image. Closes #123004. ## Problem The `stretch_shrink` scale was hard-coded in four places: `SubViewportContainer::gui_input`, `Viewport::_update_mouse_over`, `SubViewport::get_screen_transform_internal` and `SubViewport::get_popup_base_transform`. A container that draws its viewport anywhere other than the top-left corner at native size (letterboxed, integer-scaled, flipped) had no way to tell the engine. Scripts could remap pushed events, but hover tracking reads the mouse position from the DisplayServer and ignores pushed events, so hover stayed wrong. ## Change The four sites now call `SubViewportContainer::get_child_viewport_transform()`, the transform from child viewport coordinates to container local coordinates. It is a C++ virtual, exposed to scripts and GDExtension as `_get_child_viewport_transform()`. Default is unchanged: scale by `stretch_shrink` when `stretch` is on, identity otherwise. Fix for the #123004 reproduction project: ```gdscript extends SubViewportContainer # Material flips the image horizontally. Report the same flip to the engine. func _get_child_viewport_transform() -> Transform2D: return Transform2D(Vector2(-1, 0), Vector2(0, 1), Vector2(size.x, 0)) ``` ## Example Project [subviewport_container_child_transform.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33419289/subviewport_container_child_transform.zip) | scene | before | after | | :---- | :---- | :---- | | letterbox_demo.tscn | | | | issue_123004.tscn | | | ### `letterbox_demo.tscn` The letterbox demo uses a `SubViewportContainer` subclass with `stretch` off that draws its 320x200 `SubViewport` integer-scaled and centered with black bars, and overrides `_get_child_viewport_transform()` to return the same transform it draws with. Three markers show whether the engine agrees with the drawing: a yellow crosshair drawn inside the `SubViewport` at `get_local_mouse_position()` should sit under the cursor, the button should highlight on hover and print when clicked, and a red circle drawn in the root canvas at the button's `get_screen_transform()` should sit on the drawn button. Resizing the window changes the scale and bars and everything should stay aligned. Commenting out the override leaves the image unchanged but moves the crosshair, hover and red circle to the unscaled top-left position, which is what the engine did before this change. ### `issue_123004.tscn` The flipped viewport demo (`issue_123004.tscn`) mirrors the reproduction project from #123004: a stretched `SubViewportContainer` whose material flips the image horizontally, containing a rect that turns blue while hovered, red when not, and prints when clicked. The fix is to override the `_get_child_viewport_transform()` and return the same horizontal flip. The original report remapped mouse events by hand in `_gui_input` and pushed them into the viewport, which fixed clicks but not hover, since hover tracking uses the container transform rather than pushed events. The override replaces that code.
